Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
5:34 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a message. You open any payment app, scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. There is no card to carry, no cash to count and no change to hunt for.

It has also spread fast because it works everywhere. A tea stall, a vegetable seller and a large shop can all accept it with one printed QR code, and the seller needs no special machine. Since most people already have a smartphone and a bank account, there was very little to set up. Apps from different companies all work with each other, so you can pay a friend even if you use different apps.

Here are the three main reasons:

Speed and ease: Payments take a few seconds, at any hour, including holidays and late nights.
Free for most people: Sending money to friends or paying a shop usually costs nothing, unlike cards or some transfers.
Accepted almost everywhere: One QR code lets even the smallest seller take payments, so you can leave cash at home.

Safety also helps. Your bank details stay private, and each payment needs your PIN. Still, never share your PIN or approve a request you did not expect.
